findings.title: Nothing checks that each bank's BM25 index was built and its load was complete; if not, the bank arm silently falls back to full-text search
findings.evidence: run_5k_b.sh checks a load only with `test -s $W5K/load.json`, and does not check the small set's load at all. bench_enterprise._bm25_build (lines 252-261) catches any exception from bm25.build and returns {"error": ...} inside load.json, so load.json is still written. At query time, lexical._search falls back to full text when bm25.search returns None, and bm25.search returns None when bm25.ready() is False. ready() is False when lexical_state is stuck at 'building' or the tenant has no CURRENT under CIE_LEXICAL_INDEX_DIR (lexical.py:148-155, bm25.py:235-252). No warning is logged and nothing is counted: give-ups cover only run_bounded. The disk is at 95% (2.0 GB free), and the tantivy build is the last write of the load, so a failed build is a realistic case. The bank arm would then be measured on full-text search, not the BM25-based bank the first test used. measure_b's checks would not notice, and storage would count bm25 = 0 bytes, which also moves rule 4. load.json's `failed` and `documents` counts are not checked either. Checked OK in the same area: the env vars match between each load and its collect (b5k_lexical with cie_b5k, b5ks_lexical with cie_b5ks, fb_lexical with cie_pb). For the control tenant 06a6e697, lexical_state is 'ready' with version v1791343714260, which equals fb_lexical/06a6e697.../CURRENT, and lexical_queue is empty.
findings.fix: After each load, assert in the script that load.json has no lexical_index.error, has failed == 0, and has documents == the haystack size. For example: `$PY -c "import json,sys; l=json.load(open(sys.argv[1])); assert 'error' not in l['lexical_index'] and not l['failed'], l" $W/load.json`, for both W5K and WSM. Optionally have collect() also record bm25.ready(tenant) (or the retrieval trace's lexical engine) per question in giveups.json.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute it. I traced the code and ran a short probe, and the gap is there.

**The failure is swallowed and load.json is still written.**
- bench_enterprise._bm25_build (lines 252-261) catches any exception from bm25.build and returns {"error": ...}.
- load_full puts that dict into load.json under lexical_index, so load_bank writes the file anyway.
- run_5k_b.sh checks only `test -s $W5K/load.json`. It does not check the small set's load at all.
- Nobody reads lexical_index, failed or documents: grep finds lexical_index read only inside bench_enterprise itself.
- The sister benchmark does guard this. bench_enterprise.py:646-653 calls bm25.ready() and rebuilds the index if it is missing. memory_test and factbank_5k_b have no such step.

**The fallback is silent.**
- bm25.build first inserts lexical_state 'building' on an autocommit connection. A failure after that leaves the row at 'building'.
- Rows queued during the load (about 63k at 5k documents) are also over lexical_tail_max (20,000).
- Either way bm25.ready() is False, bm25.search returns None, and lexical._search uses full text. The only trace of this is info['engine'] = 'fts'.
- collect_evidence keeps only res.packet.items and never saves the trace. collect() counts only run_bounded give-ups. measure_b's checks (bank_errors, evidence_missing, gave_up, fact_bank_documents) cannot see the switch.
- Collecting twice does not help: both passes would be full text and identical.
- Only the control has a check (same_as_original). The new b5k and b5ks banks have nothing to compare against.

**Probe** (fb50 tenant in cie_pb, first question, read-only, rolled back):
- With CIE_LEXICAL_INDEX_DIR=fb_lexical: ready=True, trace engines ['bm25','bm25'], 59 items.
- With an empty scratch lexical dir: ready=False, engines ['fts','fts'], 88 items.
- Nothing was logged at WARNING level, and the search returned different evidence.

**Storage and load counts.** If the build fails early, storage() counts bm25 = 0 bytes, which shrinks bank_total and moves rule 4. If it fails after writing segments, the size looks normal while search still uses full text. load.json's failed and documents counts are also never checked.

**How likely.**
- The disk has 1.9 GB free (96% used) and another review is running in parallel.
- cie_erb holds two partial 5k tenants (3,776 and 960 documents), so earlier loads have been cut off on this machine.
- A full 5k bank takes several hundred MB plus WAL. The tantivy build (about 16 MB at 5k, per eval_out/bm25_5k) is the last write of the load.
- Most disk-full failures would hit Postgres first and abort through `test -s` and `set -e`. A build-only failure is less likely, but plausible.

**Why it matters before freezing.** If it happens, the bank arm, which the pre-registration calls 'the present system with its default search' (bm25 is the default lexical_engine), would be measured on full text. That changes the bank's numbers, and so rules 1, 2 and 4 and the headline, with nothing in b_report showing it. Once the script is frozen, the guard cannot be added.

**The suggested fix is cheap and correct.** After each load, assert in the script that there is no lexical_index.error, that failed == 0 and documents == the haystack size, for both W5K and WSM. Optionally also record bm25.ready or the trace engine per question.

findings.title: The 'fact_bank_documents' check in measure_b is always None (it reads a key the build report does not have)
findings.evidence: measure_b reads `{a: b.get("documents") for a, b in fbb.items()}` from factbank_build.json. bank.build returns sources/entities/facts/bytes/check, and factbank_test.build adds seconds. There is no 'documents' key: fb50/factbank_build.json is {"sources": 50, "entities": 380, "facts": 1969, "bytes": ..., "check": ..., "seconds": 0.48}. The report would show {v1: null, v2: null}, so a fact bank built from fewer documents than the haystack goes unnoticed (factbank_test._docs silently skips documents that read() cannot parse).
findings.fix: Use b.get("sources") and compare it with the haystack's document count (and with the bank's load.json documents).

verdict.reason: The finding is confirmed. In factbank_5k_b.py, measure_b at line 159 sets checks.fact_bank_documents = {a: b.get("documents") for a, b in fbb.items()}, where fbb is the parsed {factbank,factbank_v2}_build.json. In part B those files come only from `python -m cie.eval.factbank_test build` (run_5k_b.sh lines 20-21, and they are symlinked into the fb50-at-5k folder at line 66). factbank_test.build writes bank.build's return value plus "seconds". bank.build returns exactly {"sources", "entities", "facts", "bytes", "check"} (bank.py, end of build), so no "documents" key ever exists. fb50/factbank_build.json has no such key either. Running measure_b read-only on fb50 printed fact_bank_documents = {'v1': None, 'v2': None}. So the check is always null and could never flag a bank built from fewer documents than the haystack (factbank_test._docs drops documents that read() fails to parse). The fix is to read "sources" and compare it with the haystack's n_docs/documents. It does not matter for the test: this check feeds no rule in rules_b, and no number or verdict depends on it. The pre-registration's list of reported checks (bank errors, give-ups, missing evidence, evidence collected twice, control vs original) does not include it. The raw "sources" count is still recorded in the build JSON, so a short bank could be found by reading that file. What is lost is a reported integrity check, not a result.

findings.title: chance is computed for the fb50-at-5,089 folder but never reported; the report looks for the small set's chance, which is never computed
findings.evidence: The script runs `chance --work $W5K` and `chance --work $WFB`. b_test reads chance.json only for `for w in (big, small)`, so b_report has chance_b5k but no chance for b5kfb. It looks for b5ksmall/chance.json, which the script never writes. I confirmed this with a synthetic score run (scratchpad/rev5kb/score_sim): the report keys were ['chance_b5k']. The pre-registration says the per-question chance counts are reported, and the secondary set at 5,089 documents is where the recalled 0.23/0.40/0.75 figures need that context.
findings.fix: In b_test, loop over (big, fb) (or all four folders) for chance.json, or run chance on WSM too and report every one that exists.

verdict.reason: I tried to refute this and couldn't. Line 72 of run_5k_b.sh runs `chance --work $WFB` (b5kfb), and line 71 runs it on W5K. It never runs on $WSM. But b_test in cie/src/cie/eval/factbank_5k_b.py (around lines 242-245) reads chance.json only for `for w in (big, small)`. So b5kfb/chance.json gets written but is never added to b_report.json. The loop also looks for b5ksmall/chance.json, which nothing ever writes. to_markdown never prints any chance data either. I checked this with a mock: I stubbed measure_b, rules_b, same_bank_evidence, same_as_original and to_markdown, then wrote chance.json only where the script writes it (b5k and b5kfb). The report's chance keys came out as ['chance_b5k'] and nothing else. The temporary folders were in scratchpad/rev5kb/chk_chance and I deleted them; no repository files changed. This is a gap against the pre-registration. Its "Also reported" list includes the per-question `chance` counts, and its Known limits section relies on those counts for the 5,089-document case. The fb50-at-5,089 set is the one tied to the recalled 0.23/0.40/0.75 disclosure. The impact is small, though. chance is reported for information only. It feeds no rule, reach number or verdict, and b5kfb/chance.json stays on disk, so it can be read or added to the report later without rerunning anything. Fixing it is a one-line loop change.

findings.title: The control is no longer 'in its own database, as before': cie_pb now holds 5 more tenants that share its HNSW and GIN indexes
findings.evidence: fb50's evidence was written at 2026-10-07 03:29. At that time erbfull-50-c6dd93 was the only tenant in cie_pb (created 03:27). cie_pb now also holds erbfull-50-1e4908, -d85f0c, -d10d57, erbfull-49-4dd4d4 and -a96489 (created 05:01-05:35), about 2,900 more records and 2,300 more sections in the shared halfvec HNSW, trigram and tsv indexes. The control tenant's own rows are unchanged: per-table pg_column_size is 64849 / 951652 / 1548800 / 103152 / 0, identical to fb50/evidence_info.json, and max(recorded_at) is 03:27. Memory bank, retrieval and memory_test code are unchanged since then (git log). But the HNSW graph (approximate, with iterative_scan relaxed_order), planner statistics and the timing of the bounded ent_sim and lex_tier queries now differ from the original run. Any difference that same_as_original reports would be read as 'today's code' when the code did not change. Checked OK: the fact bank v1 rebuilt today on fb50 (scratch) gives identical answers and evidence to fb50/factbank.jsonl.
findings.fix: Say this in the pre-registration and the script comment: other tenants were added to cie_pb after the original run. Attribute differences to the code only if none appear. Alternatively, re-collect the control in a fresh database holding only a reload of fb50 (that changes the bank, so disclose whichever choice is made).

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute this and couldn't. The finding is confirmed with a reproduction, though the mechanism is different from the one the reviewer named.

Facts: cie_pb holds 6 tenants. erbfull-50-c6dd93 was created at 03:27. Five more were created between 05:01 and 05:35, with 505 to 630 records each. Each tenant has its own BM25 directory and no rows are queued. Git log shows no change to retrieval, memory or memory_test.py since 10-05. The script comment says 'in its own database, as before', and that is now false.

Probes, all in scratchpad/rev5kb, bank arm only, about 18 s each:
1. I re-collected the fb50 control on cie_pb with today's code (PYTHONHASHSEED=0, fb_lexical). The bank evidence differs from fb50/evidence.jsonl on 6 of 50 questions: github_author-001, github_author-005, metadata-qst_0050, linear_due-002, metadata-qst_0087, metadata-qst_0043. The differences are a few items swapped or reordered at positions 20 and later. There were 0 give-ups and 0 errors.
2. The result repeats exactly on a second run and under hash seeds 1, 2 and 3.
3. Forcing an exact vector search (index and bitmap scans off) gives the same result as the HNSW search. So the HNSW graph and iterative_scan are not the cause.
4. The cause is pipeline.py:184. The graph-expansion budget is ceil(4*log2(N)), and N is pg_class.reltuples for the whole memory_records table, which every tenant shares. reltuples is now 3400, so the budget is 47. With the control alone it would be about 580, so 37.
5. I monkeypatched budget_for to use N=580. Today's code then reproduces the original bank evidence and bank_blocks exactly on all 50 questions (0 differences). With N=16 it gives 9 different differences.

So same_as_original(b5kfb50) would report 6 bank differences. Under the pre-registration's wording ('re-collected with today's code', with retrieval code unchanged) they would be blamed on the code. In fact the other tenants inflate reltuples.

Impact: the pre-registered 'control against original run' check would show 6 differences where the true answer is 0, with the wrong explanation. The fb50 control's bank arm also runs with a bigger graph budget than the original run had. On these 50 questions this does not change the bank's reach at 2,000, 6,000 or 24,000 characters (I checked with reachable). It does not touch any primary rule either: the rules use the 5k and small-set banks, each in a new database of its own, and rule 5 uses the fact bank's direct answers.

Fix: before freezing, disclose that 5 tenants were added to cie_pb. Say that the graph budget follows table-wide reltuples, so differences come from that and not from the code. Alternatively, re-collect the control in a database that holds only this bank.

findings.title: The 5,089-document load writes into eval_out/enterprise_full/emb_cache.sqlite through the symlink
findings.evidence: CachedEmbedder (ingest/bulk.py:79-121) opens the path read-write with sqlite3.connect. It runs CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS and then INSERT OR IGNORE plus commit for every miss. Only the main process writes, and SQLite 3.45 resolves the symlink for its journal, so existing entries are not overwritten or corrupted. But an earlier artifact (84 MB, untouched since Sep 24) gains the new section, record and profile texts (about 1.4k to 7k). Hits do occur: keys are sha1(model_name + NUL + text) with model_name 'BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5'. 515 of fb50's 1,055 cache keys are present in eval_out's cache, and all 515 vectors are byte-identical. Minor side note on 'only the time changes': hits return fp16-rounded vectors to the in-memory link, same-object and near-duplicate decisions (bulk.py _unit_vectors, _cos, _near_duplicates), while misses use full float32. The small set's bank and the original fb50 load were all misses. The stored halfvec vectors are identical either way; only decisions within about 1e-4 of a threshold could flip.
findings.fix: Copy the cache (`cp`, 84 MB) instead of symlinking it, or open it read-only, so eval_out stays untouched. Otherwise state in the pre-registration that the shared cache is extended.

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute this and could not; the mechanism holds. Line 48 of run_5k_b.sh runs `ln -sf $PWD/eval_out/enterprise_full/emb_cache.sqlite $W5K/emb_cache.sqlite`. memory_test.load_bank then passes cache=(local or work)/"emb_cache.sqlite" to bench_enterprise.load_full. That reaches CachedEmbedder (bulk.py:79-121), which opens the file read-write with sqlite3.connect, runs CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, and does INSERT OR IGNORE plus commit for every miss. The design note understand_b.json recommended `cp eval_out/enterprise_full/emb_cache.sqlite $W/emb_cache.sqlite`, so the symlink is a departure from the design.

Checks I ran:
- A throwaway probe in rev5kb/symprobe (a symlink to a fresh sqlite file, a dummy embedder, SQLite 3.45.1) wrote 2 rows into the real target. No journal was left next to the symlink.
- A read-only check confirmed eval_out's cache has 77,860 entries. 515 of fb50's 1,055 keys are in it, and all 515 vectors are byte-identical.
- eval_out's file is still unmodified (mtime Sep 24, 84,168,704 bytes).

It does not matter for the test:
- eval_out/ is gitignored (cie/.gitignore:11), so this is a local artifact, not a tracked file.
- INSERT OR IGNORE never overwrites existing entries, and only the main process writes.
- Only W5K uses this cache. WSM gets a fresh cache of its own, and WFB/WFB50 do not load a bank.
- A copy and a symlink give the 5,089 load exactly the same hits and vectors, so no part B number, verdict or fairness depends on which one is used.
- The fp16 side note (hits return fp16-rounded vectors to the in-memory link and near-duplicate decisions, misses return float32) applies equally to a copy. It is not caused by the symlink. It only nuances the pre-registration's wording "only the time changes", and could flip decisions only within about 1e-4 of a threshold.

The only effect is housekeeping: an earlier artifact gains a few thousand entries. Switching to `cp`, as the design note said, or noting this in the pre-registration, would be tidy but is optional.

findings.title: Re-running the script after a failure silently replaces the control's first pass with a no-op, then stops at createdb
findings.evidence: On a rerun, the first collect in twice() finds a complete evidence.jsonl from the previous second pass. memory_test.collect_evidence skips every question already present (`done`/`todo`), so it collects nothing and writes giveups.json = {gave_up: 0}. `mv` then overwrites evidence_pass1.jsonl with the earlier warm pass, and `cp` sets giveups_pass1.json to 0. Step 2's `createdb` then fails because cie_b5k already exists, and set -e aborts. The result is a control whose 'first pass' and pass-1 give-ups are no longer real. On a single clean run, twice() behaves as intended: evidence.jsonl is absent before the second collect, so all 50 questions are re-collected. Checked OK elsewhere: bash -n passes; createdb as postgres plus `cie.cli migrate` on a fresh database reach head b0c1d2e3f4a5 with vector 0.8.1 and pg_trgm, and the index set is identical to cie_pb's (tested on a throwaway database, since dropped); ensure_indexes finds nothing missing; find_loaded_tenant cannot pick a wrong tenant in the fresh databases; the checkpoints loop and wait use the right PID; the give-up handler counts run_bounded's 'bounded query %s gave up ...' DEBUG record on logger cie.retrieval.bounded (probed: n=1, by_query lex_tier=1); the score step runs end to end on synthetic folders; asking never writes to a fact bank, so the WFB symlinks to W5K's banks are safe.
findings.fix: Make twice() refuse to run if evidence_pass1.jsonl already exists, or skip the folder when both passes exist. Use `createdb ... || true` together with a check that the database is empty, or document that a failed run must start from fresh folders and databases.

verdict.reason: I could not refute it. Each step checks out against the code. In run_5k_b.sh, twice() runs collect, then `mv evidence.jsonl evidence_pass1.jsonl` and `cp giveups.json giveups_pass1.json`, then runs collect again. memory_test.collect_evidence (lines 804-806) skips every question already in evidence.jsonl that has all three arms. I ran that done/todo logic on fb50's 50-row evidence.jsonl, which has the same shape a previous pass 2 leaves: 50 questions, 50 done, 0 to do. So on a rerun the first collect gathers nothing. factbank_5k_b.collect still writes giveups.json as {gave_up: 0}, and the mv/cp then overwrite the real cold pass 1 and its give-ups with the earlier warm pass 2. `su postgres -c "createdb -O cie cie_pb"` on an existing database exits 1 ("already exists"), and under set -e that stops the script. One correction to the finding: the rerun only stops at createdb if the first run got as far as step 2. If it failed earlier (in step 0's facts or in step 1), the rerun creates the databases and carries on, and the control's pass 1 is replaced silently. Impact is small. The scored pass is unaffected: the second collect starts from an absent evidence.jsonl and re-collects all 50, and its giveups.json is real. The rules and the verdict (measure_b, rules_b, replace) never read evidence_pass1.jsonl, and nothing reads giveups_pass1.json at all. Only the reported check bank_evidence_twice (same_bank_evidence) would compare two warm passes instead of a cold one and a warm one, and only after a failed run that is restarted without cleanup. This is a robustness issue in the run script, not a test-number issue.

findings.title: b_test leaves out the load and build times that 'Also reported' promises
findings.evidence: The pre-registration's 'Also reported' list (FACTBANK_5K_B_PREREGISTRATION.md lines 106-107) includes 'the load and build times'. Nothing in factbank_5k_b.py reads load.json (load_seconds, embed_seconds, finish_seconds, lexical_index.seconds) or plain_meta.json (bm25_seconds, embed_seconds). measure_b does read factbank_build.json and factbank_v2_build.json into `fbb`, but it keeps only `bytes` and `documents` and drops `seconds`. So b_report.json and b_report.md hold no load or build time for any of the four folders. The numbers exist only in the work folders' files. Timing per question (median, p90, max) and storage are reported.
findings.fix: In measure_b, add a 'times' block: load.json's load_seconds, embed_seconds and finish_seconds; plain_meta.json's bm25_seconds and embed_seconds; and each factbank*_build.json's seconds. Print it in to_markdown.

verdict.reason: I could not refute it. The pre-registration's "Also reported" list (line 106) promises "the load and build times". In factbank_5k_b.py, measure_b reads only questions.jsonl, evidence.jsonl, factbank*.jsonl, evidence_info.json (storage), factbank*_build.json and giveups.json. It never opens load.json or plain_meta.json. From `fbb` it keeps only `bytes` (under storage) and `documents` (under checks), so the `seconds` field that factbank_test.build writes (line 104) is dropped. evidence_info.json comes from memory_test.storage, which holds bytes only, no times. b_test and to_markdown add no times either. So b_report.json and b_report.md would hold no load or build time for any folder. Part A does it differently: factbank_5k.py line 379 puts each build's `seconds` into a `builds` block. That makes part B's omission an inconsistency, not a deliberate choice. It does not matter for the test. The times are still written to the work folders: load.json has load_seconds, embed_seconds, finish_seconds and lexical_index.seconds (fb50/load.json has them, e.g. load_seconds 71.4), plain_meta.json has bm25_seconds and embed_seconds, and factbank*_build.json has seconds. Nothing is lost, they can be added to the report after the run, and no rule, verdict, number or comparison depends on them.

findings.title: The chance counts for fb50 at 5,089 documents are computed but never reach the report; b_test looks for a small-set file that is never made
findings.evidence: run_5k_b.sh step 7 runs `chance` on $W5K and $WFB. b_test only reads chance.json from `(big, small)` (lines 242-245), so it picks up chance_b5k and looks for chance_b5ksmall, which the script never computes. $WFB/chance.json (the fb50 questions at 5,089 documents) is written but left out of b_report. The pre-registration promises 'for each question, how many other documents carry the answer's text (chance)' and names fb50 at 5,089 as one of the four reported folders.
findings.fix: In b_test, read chance.json from (big, fb), or from all four folders when present. Or run chance on the folders that b_test reads. Also print a per-group median of the chance counts in to_markdown.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed by reading the code and running a probe. Step 7 of run_5k_b.sh runs `chance` only on $W5K (b5k) and $WFB (b5kfb). b_test (factbank_5k_b.py, the loop `for w in (big, small)` near line 242) reads chance.json only from big and small. So the report picks up chance_b5k and looks for b5ksmall/chance.json, which nothing ever writes. The fb50-at-5,089 counts in $WFB/chance.json are written but never reach b_report.json. to_markdown prints no chance data at all.

Probe: I built four dummy folders under scratchpad/rev5kb/chanceprobe with the test fixture's layout, put chance.json in big and fb only (as the script does), and called F.b_test. The report's chance keys were only ['chance_big'], and b_report.md does not contain the word 'chance'.

So the finding is accurate. It does not affect the test, though. chance is information listed under 'Also reported'. It feeds no rule, number or verdict: rules_b, replace and the reach figures are all independent of it. The primary questions' counts still reach the JSON report. The fb50-at-5,089 counts are still on disk in $WFB/chance.json, and the design investigation's own chance.json also covers them. chance depends only on the haystack and the questions, so it can be recomputed or added to the report after the run with no effect on any result. This is a reporting gap that is worth fixing (read chance from fb as well, and print a per-group median in the markdown), but leaving it as is would not change a number, a verdict or the fairness of the test.

findings.title: chance() does not count the same way as reachable(): it over-counts pull request numbers and under-counts dates and some names
findings.evidence: chance() matches `(?<!\w)value(?!\w)` on _norm(json.dumps(raw)) for every kind. reachable() uses dates_in for dates (ISO plus written-out forms), ids_in for keys and pull request numbers (KEY_RE, and PR_RE, which skips digits after '-', '.' or '/'), and the regex only for values. I ran both on fb50's 50 questions over all 5,089 mt5k documents, counting with reachable(q, render_doc(doc)) > 0 (rev5kb/chance_cmp.py). (1) Pull request numbers are over-counted: github_author-001 gives 17 from chance() against 1 from reachable, because '4827' matches inside 'eng-4827'. The github_author median is 3 against 0. (2) Dates are under-counted: written-out dates such as 'Thu, 9 Dec 2026' are missed. action_due-021 gives 3 against 10; the action_due median is 6.5 against 10; 7 of 10 linear_due questions differ. (3) A value just after a newline is missed, because json.dumps writes the newline as the two characters backslash and 'n', and the 'n' breaks the word boundary: Markus Klein gives 85 against 89. For lists, chance also counts a document that holds any one of the expected ids. chance() does find the answer in every gold document, so the counts are biased but not empty.
findings.fix: Count with the measure's own check: sum(dsid not in gold and reachable(q, text) > 0), with text = title + render_doc, or title + raw. For lists, also report how many documents hold each id, or the best share.

verdict.reason:
The finding is correct. I could not refute it. In cie/src/cie/eval/factbank_5k_b.py:203-219, chance() runs one regex, `(?<!\w)value(?!\w)`, over _norm(json.dumps(raw)) for every kind of question. The measure works differently. reachable() in factbank_test.py:144-154 checks dates with dates_in (ISO dates plus written-out dates) and lists with ids_in. For pull requests ids_in uses PR_RE, which skips digits that come right after '-', '.' or '/', and a list scores the share of its ids found. Only plain values use the regex.

I ran the real chance() on a copy of mt5k's haystack.json and index.json plus fb50's questions.jsonl, in rev5kb/vchance. I then counted the same documents with reachable(q, render_doc(doc)) > 0 (script rev5kb/vchance.py, results in rows.json). Every number in the finding came out the same:
- **Pull request numbers are over-counted.** github_author-001 gives 17 against 1, because '4827' matches inside 'eng-4827'. The github_author median is 3 against 0, and 4 of the 5 questions differ.
- **Dates are under-counted.** action_due-021 gives 3 against 10. The action_due median is 6.5 against 10, and 7 of the 10 linear_due questions differ by 1 to 3.
- **Names after a newline are missed.** json.dumps writes a newline as backslash plus 'n', and that 'n' breaks the word boundary. Markus Klein gives 85 against 89.

The design investigation (understand_b.json:186) counted with the measure's own checks, dates_in and ids_in, and found "the pull request lists are clean: each expected number appears in at most 1 other document." The code as written would report up to 17 for the same lists, so it does not follow the method that motivated it.

Effect on the test: chance only feeds the chance_* fields of b_report.json. It does not feed the rules, the replace verdict or any arm's reach. But it is a pre-registered output: the preregistration's "Also reported" list and its Known limits section ("The chance counts show how much"). As written, it would report wrong exposure counts. They overstate the list group by up to 17 times and understate deadlines, the group the preregistration says is most exposed. The fix is cheap and should go in before the code is frozen: count with sum(dsid not in gold and reachable(q, title + render_doc) > 0). This is low severity, and no verdict changes.

findings.title: The 'used' set matches by id, but mt50's generated ids name different questions: 4 never-used questions are dropped
findings.evidence: mt50's questions were generated on its own 36-document haystack, so its ids restart at 001. 12 of its 23 ids are mt5k ids that name different questions (for example, mt50 linear_due-001 is 'Data Sovereignty Routing Mosaic...' while mt5k linear_due-001 is 'Mitigate asymmetric NAT...'). Matching on kind, expected answer and gold docs: none of mt50's generated questions is an mt5k question, so nothing used leaks in. But mt5k's linear_due-004, action_due-001, action_due-004 and linear_due_window-001 are left out only because of the id clash. As a result the unused, non-flawed pools are owners 47, linear_due 19, action_due 10 and lists 32. Matching by content gives 20 / 12 / 33, which agrees with understand_b's 20 Linear due dates and 12 action items. The action_due draw takes 8 of only 10. fbtest's 44 reworded questions keep mt5k's ids, expected answers and gold docs, so for fbtest the id match is right. A scan of every questions*.jsonl under the scratchpad found none of the 108 candidates anywhere else. The draw does give exactly 26 / 10 / 8 / 6 with no used, flawed or duplicate ids for seeds 1, 2, 3, 100 and 999. The FLAWED ids all exist, all are unused list questions, and they match my recomputation exactly: these 10, and only these, miss a reused key.
findings.fix: In `questions`, match used questions by (kind, expected, gold_docs) rather than by id, or by id only where the question text also matches mt5k's. Otherwise state in the pre-registration that the 4 clashing ids are excluded, and give the pool sizes (47 / 19 / 10 / 32).

verdict.reason:
I could not refute it. The CLI builds `used` from ids only (factbank_5k_b.py:294), and draw_questions drops anything whose id is in that set (line 56). mt50's questions were generated on its own 36-document haystack, so its generated ids start again at 001. Of mt50's 23 ids, 12 also exist in mt5k but carry different content. fb50 (50 of 50) and fbtest (46 of 46) match mt5k on both id and content, so the id match is right for those two.

Four mt5k questions are dropped only because of the id clash: action_due-001, action_due-004, linear_due-004 and linear_due_window-001. None of them is in fb50 or fbtest, and none of their question texts appears in mt50.

Unused, non-flawed pool sizes:
- Matching by id: owners 47, linear_due 19, action_due 10, lists 32.
- Matching by content: owners 47, linear_due 20, action_due 12, lists 33.

The content figures agree with understand_b.json, the design investigation: 20 Linear due dates and 12 action items unused, 43 lists, and only 10 mt50 questions used. So the code silently differs from the design's count and from the pre-registration's wording that the frame is the questions "no earlier test used".

One detail in the finding is wrong. It says none of mt50's generated questions is an mt5k question, but two are, word for word: mt50 action_due-001 is mt5k action_due-027, and mt50 action_due-004 is mt5k action_due-015. Both are already in fb50, so nothing used leaks into the draw either way.

The draws with seeds 1, 2 and 3 each give 26/10/8/6, with 50 distinct ids and none of them used. When I fixed the used set to match by content, 2 or 3 of the 4 dropped questions were drawn in each seed, and the draw shared 36 to 41 of its 50 questions with the id-based draw.

Why it should not change the test: the four questions are dropped because of an id clash, not because of anything to do with how hard they are or how either system does on them. No used question gets in, and the sample is still a valid seeded random sample of a slightly smaller pool (action_due takes 8 of 10 rather than 8 of 12). Fixing it changes which questions are drawn, not whether the result is fair, and the verdict is unaffected in expectation. Still, seed 61 cannot be redrawn once it is run, so before freezing either match by content or add one line to the pre-registration naming the four excluded ids and the pool sizes 47/19/10/32.

findings.title: checks.fact_bank_documents is always None: it reads 'documents', but the build report's key is 'sources'
findings.evidence: measure_b sets `"fact_bank_documents": {a: b.get("documents") ...}`. cie.factbank.bank.build returns {"sources", "entities", "facts", "bytes", "check"} (bank.py:256), and fb50/factbank_build.json has "sources": 50. Running measure_b on a copy of fb50 gave 'fact_bank_documents': {'v1': None, 'v2': None}. So the check that each fact bank was built from all 5,089 documents, or from the small set, never shows anything.
findings.fix: Use b.get("sources"), and compare it with haystack.json's n documents.

verdict.reason: I tried to refute this and couldn't. measure_b (src/cie/eval/factbank_5k_b.py:159) sets fact_bank_documents to b.get("documents") for each *_build.json. Those files are written only by cie.eval.factbank_test.build (factbank_test.py:105), which saves whatever cie.factbank.bank.build returns. That report has the keys sources, entities, facts, bytes and check (bank.py:256), plus seconds. There is no "documents" key, and fb50/factbank_build.json has "sources": 50. run_5k_b.sh builds every fact bank through this same factbank_test build path, so no other writer could add the key. I copied fb50/factbank_build.json into a scratch folder with one question and ran measure_b. It returned checks.fact_bank_documents = {'v1': None}, so the field is always None. It does not change a test number or verdict. The field goes only into the 'checks' line of the write-up. rules_b does not read it, and the pre-registration's list of checks does not include it. Each run folder keeps its *_build.json with the real "sources" count, so the number of documents behind each fact bank can still be checked by hand against haystack.json. The fix is to read b.get("sources").

findings.title: Rule 1 handles a missing bank group mean differently from factbank_test.score; otherwise rules 1-4 and 'replace' match
findings.evidence: I copied fb50's evidence.jsonl, factbank*.jsonl, evidence_info.json and factbank*_build.json to rev5kb/fb50c and ran both score and measure_b. Reach for all 4 arms, 3 budgets and every group plus the mean, per question and per group, and the own answers (0.654 / 1.0 / 1.0 / 0.885) are identical, and equal to the stored factbank_report.json. rules_b gives the same rules 1-4 (met, met, met, not met). Rule 4 uses bank_total (rows plus BM25) against factbank_build bytes, as score does. 'replace' is rules[0], [1] and [3], which are rules 1, 2 and 4. Rule 5 is v1's own answers at 5,089 minus the small set's, >= -0.05, as written. One difference remains: score's rule 1 uses `(d(...) or 0) >= -0.03`, so a group where the bank's mean is None but the fact bank's is not counts as a pass. rules_b requires `x is not None`, so the same case fails. This can only happen if the bank has no evidence for a whole group, which checks.evidence_missing would also show.
findings.fix: Either keep score's `or 0` so the rule is literally unchanged, or note in the pre-registration that a missing bank group fails rule 1.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute it. The code difference is real, but it only shows up in a run that would already be broken.

1. **The two rule 1 checks differ.** factbank_test.score (src/cie/eval/factbank_test.py:205) uses `all((d(fb24, bk24, g) or 0) >= -0.03 for g in GROUPS if fb24.get(g) is not None)`. When the bank's group mean is None, `d` returns None, `or 0` turns that into 0, and the group passes. factbank_5k_b.rules_b (src/cie/eval/factbank_5k_b.py:172) requires `(x := d(...)) is not None and x >= -0.03`, so the same group fails.

2. **Synthetic check.** I set the bank's 24,000 'lists' mean to None and the fact bank's to 0.8. rules_b gave rule 1 = False and the score-style expression gave True. The other rules agree on None: rule 2 and rule 3 both come out False either way, and rule 4 uses bank_total against the factbank_build bytes in both. Replace is rules 1, 2 and 4 in both.

3. **Reproduction.** On the reviewer's copy rev5kb/fb50c, measure_b plus rules_b give [True, True, True, False]. That matches the stored fb50 factbank_report.json rules ([True, True, True, False], replace False). The bank reach at 24,000 is owners 0.808, deadlines 0.5, lists 0.583, and evidence_missing is 0.

4. **When a bank group mean can be None.** A bank error does not cause it: memory_test.collect_evidence records a failed search as an empty packet, so `row['bank']` is the empty string (bank_error is set too). measure_b then still scores reach as 0, not None. A None mean needs every question in a group to have no 'bank' evidence at all (missing rows or a missing key). That means collection was incomplete, which checks.evidence_missing would report and which makes the run invalid anyway.

The pre-registration says the rules are "the first test's rules, unchanged", so the code literally differs from the document. But in any valid run this cannot change a number or a verdict. Of the two behaviours, failing the group (rules_b) is the safer one.

findings.title: The time p90 takes the rank one above nearest-rank
findings.evidence: _ms uses xs[min(n-1, int(0.9*n))]; for n=50 that is xs[45], the 46th value. Nearest-rank p90 is xs[44]. On fb50's bank timings, _ms reports 187.2 ms where nearest-rank gives 184.0 ms. This is cosmetic for a 'time per question' line, but the method should be stated or fixed before the freeze.
findings.fix: Use xs[math.ceil(0.9*n) - 1], or statistics.quantiles(xs, n=10)[-1], and state which one.

verdict.reason:
The facts in the finding are correct, but the formula is a valid percentile method, not an error. In /home/user/integratedai/cie/src/cie/eval/factbank_5k_b.py:112, _ms returns xs[min(n-1, int(0.9*n))]. Both question sets have n=50, so that is xs[45], the 46th smallest value. Nearest-rank p90 would be xs[44].

I ran this on fb50/evidence.jsonl:
- bank: _ms gives p90 187.2; nearest-rank gives 184.0; numpy's default method gives 184.3; statistics.quantiles(n=10) gives 186.9.
- plain: 15.4 against 15.3.
- plain-words: 0.7 under every method.

So the reported numbers match the finding exactly. understand_b.json quotes 184.0 for the same fb50 data, which is not what the code would print.

Why it is not an error: xs[int(0.9n)] is the same as numpy's percentile(method='higher') for n=50 (both give index 45; method='inverted_cdf' gives 44). It is the upper of the two values that every common percentile method falls between. Part A uses the same formula (src/cie/eval/factbank_5k.py:333), so parts A and B already agree. Changing B alone, as the suggested fix does, would make the two parts use different methods. Neither pre-registration says which method it uses; both just say "90th percentile".

Effect on the test: none. Timing goes only into the 'time per question' report line. rules_b and the verdicts never read ms, so no score, verdict or fairness changes. The right fix is to name the method in the pre-registration (or change A and B together), not just B.

findings.title: The 50-document control (fb50) would be re-collected in cie_pb, where it is no longer alone, and the bank's graph budget has changed since the original run
findings.evidence:
run_5k_b.sh:28 says the control is re-collected 'in its own database, as before', and line 33 runs `twice $WFB50 cie_pb $S/fb_lexical`. cie_pb now holds 6 tenants. erbfull-50-c6dd93 was created at 03:27 on Oct 7 and fb50/evidence.jsonl was written at 03:29. The other five tenants (1e4908, d85f0c, d10d57, 4dd4d4, a96489) were created between 05:01 and 05:35, and no orphan rows exist, so c6dd93 was alone when the original evidence was collected.

The bank's search depends on the whole database, not only the tenant. pipeline.py:183-185 sets the graph-expansion budget from `SELECT reltuples FROM pg_class WHERE relname='memory_records'`, which counts every tenant. cie_pb's reltuples is now 3,400 (3,469 actual rows), so graph.budget_for gives 47 to 48. At the original run it was 35 (403 records: load_full runs ANALYZE before _link_entities adds people, companies and projects) or 37 (580 records). Expanded records feed the candidates and the packet, so the bank's evidence for the control is likely to differ from Oct 7.

Two more things changed. The HNSW index and the planner statistics are shared with the other tenants. The original run probably did not set PYTHONHASHSEED.

This breaks the pre-registration's own reasoning (lines 60-61): each size's bank must be alone in its database. The primary small set gets that (cie_b5ks); the fb50 control does not. The comparison with the original run will then show differences the pre-registration does not expect ('the memory bank, retrieval and memory-test code have not changed').

What I checked and found fine: the lexical index is not affected. c6dd93's tantivy folder in fb_lexical is unchanged since 03:28 on Oct 7, lexical_state is 'ready', the queue is empty, and BM25 is per tenant. git log 8375901..HEAD shows no change to retrieval, memory, ingest, core, alembic, memory_test, bench_enterprise or bench_scale.
findings.fix: Re-collect the fb50 control in a fresh database at the current schema, as for the primary small set. Load fb50's 50 documents; fb50/emb_cache.sqlite makes this cheap. Alternatively, copy cie_pb (CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE cie_pb), delete the other five tenants and run ANALYZE. Then compare the result with the Oct 7 evidence. In the pre-registration, say that the re-collected evidence is the control and list the known reasons it may differ from the original run (graph budget 35 to 37 then, hash seed). Correct the comment at run_5k_b.sh:28.

verdict.reason:
I tried to refute this and could not; a direct probe confirms it.

Code: memory_test.collect_evidence calls Retriever.retrieve with the default use_graph=True. pipeline.py:183-185 sets the graph budget as graph.budget_for(reltuples of memory_records, 4.0). That reltuples counts the whole table, not one tenant.

cie_pb today: reltuples is 3400, so the budget is ceil(4*log2(3400)) = 47. The database holds 6 tenants. erbfull-50-c6dd93 (580 records) was created at 03:27:22 on Oct 7. fb50/load.json was written at 03:28:34 and fb50/evidence.jsonl at 03:29:21. The other five tenants were created between 05:01 and 05:35, so c6dd93 was alone at the original run. bench_enterprise.py:404 runs ANALYZE before _link_entities adds the 177 person, organization and project records. reltuples was therefore 403 or 580 then, a budget of 35 or 37.

Probe (scratchpad/rev5kb/probe_budget.py): read-only, every search rolled back, 10 fb50 questions taken every 5th. I ran the bank's search in cie_pb as run_5k_b.sh would: fastembed, fb_lexical, PYTHONHASHSEED=0.
- At the current budget of 47, the bank's evidence differs from the original evidence.jsonl on 2 of 10 questions (github_author-001, linear_due-002).
- A warm-up pass gives the same result, so warming up does not explain the gap.
- With only the budget forced back to 37 or 35, all 10 questions match the original exactly.

So the budget is the cause. The HNSW index, the planner statistics and the hash seed are not, at least on this sample.

Consequences:
- run_5k_b.sh:28 says the control runs "in its own database, as before". That is false.
- The pre-registration (lines 51-54, 60-61) expects the re-collected control to reproduce the original, since "the memory bank, retrieval and memory-test code have not changed". same_as_original (control_against_original_run) would instead report bank differences that come from the shared database, not the code.
- The control's bank evidence also feeds the reported fb50_50 bank numbers and change_fb50_5k_minus_50.

It does not affect the primary rules. rules_fb50_5k does not depend on the control's bank evidence either: rule 5 uses only the fact bank's own answers. The fix the finding proposes is sound: a fresh database or a template copy with the other tenants removed and ANALYZE run.

findings.title: Give-ups and bank errors are only counted, with no action fixed in advance, and they only ever hurt the bank
findings.evidence:
collect() counts the bounded queries that gave up. In collect_evidence, a failed retrieve leaves bank='' plus bank_error, and measure_b then scores '' as reach 0. Only the bank arm has time limits: ent_sim 400 ms, lexical tiers 4,000 and 1,500 ms, failures logged only at debug level. So any give-up or error lowers the bank's score and helps the fact bank on rules 1 and 2.

The pre-registration's own reading says rule 1's -0.03 is less than one question in owners (0.038) or deadlines (0.056). A single silent give-up in the scored second pass can therefore decide rule 1. 'Runs after part A, on an idle machine' is a promise that run_5k_b.sh does not check, and nothing in the pre-registration says what happens when give-ups or bank errors are greater than 0.
findings.fix: Pre-register a gate. If the scored pass has any give-up or bank_error, re-collect the affected questions, or the whole pass, with the machine idle before scoring. If they persist, report rules 1 and 2 with and without those questions. Have the script record the load average, or refuse to start while Part A is still running.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute the core claim. Checked against the code and with short probes:
(1) The pre-registration only counts and reports give-ups and bank errors (lines 67-68 and 107). No action is fixed for a count above 0: no re-collection, no exclusion, no scoring with and without those questions. Part A's pre-registration has no general gate either. run_5k_b.sh does not check that the machine is idle or that Part A has finished. The design critic in understand_b.json asked for exactly this gate ('required to be 0, or the question rerun with the CPUs free'), and the draft adopted only the counting.
(2) The mechanism is as described. collect_evidence catches any retrieve exception and writes bank='' plus bank_error. measure_b keeps '' because it is not None, and reachable(q, '') returns 0.0. The resume logic counts that row as done, so it is never retried. run_bounded returns None on timeout and logs at DEBUG only. I confirmed _GiveUps does count a forced timeout ({'ent_sim': 1}). The plain arms and the fact bank (sqlite) have no query time limits, so only the bank is exposed.
(3) Give-ups are plausible at this size. On the 5,000-document tenant erbfull-5000-9688c2 in cie_erb (33k of the database's 83k records, under moderate load), the 400 ms ent_sim query ran for 33 of the 50 fb50 questions. Median was about 195 ms, and 3 to 4 runs went over 400 ms even on a warm second pass. One question where the query returns a useful hit (linear_due-026, sim > 0.35) took 410 ms. The pre-registration's own reading says one owner or deadline question decides rule 1.
Where the finding overstates:
- The lexical tier limits (4,000 and 1,500 ms) do not apply. The bank uses the BM25 engine on a ready index, so only ent_sim is bounded.
- The slowest give-ups are short generic spans ('US and EU', 'In the P1 Sev1') that match no rows anyway, so giving up on them changes nothing.
- Part B's database holds only the one tenant, about 2.4 times fewer rows, so the queries that matter should run around 150 to 200 ms on an idle machine.
- 'Only ever hurt' is mostly but not strictly true.
So a decisive give-up is unlikely on an idle machine but possible under the contention this shared 4-CPU box shows now (ollama and other reviews are running). A raw count cannot tell harmless give-ups from harmful ones, which is why an action fixed in advance is needed. It has to be added before freezing to avoid a decision made after seeing the results.

findings.title: The disclosure that the haystack was seen leaves out how much the fact bank was exposed to it, and calls it the only option
findings.evidence:
Lines 28-31 say the memory bank's search was developed on mt5k and that 'the fact bank's first test drew from it'. Also true:
- The multi-document development sets lie inside mt5k: mdtrain 50 of 50 documents, mdtest 49 of 49, mdchanged 49 of 49, as do mdtrainall and mdtrainv9.
- The v1 builder changed during that work: bank.py adds a '#<pr>' alias for every GitHub document (commit 44a880f, after the first test's 8375901). The engine also changed.
- Part A's probes and dry run already ran v1 on mt5k at 5,089 documents (u5k/scale ans_v1, dry_run.json), on other questions.
- For the primary set, v2's lessons (fb50) use the same question templates, for example 'due'. The questions lens noted this, but the pre-registration flags v2 as in-sample only for the secondary set.

'It is the only haystack where owner questions with checkable answers exist' is true of the haystacks that exist. But mt5k itself was built as a base plus planted metadata gold documents, and an unseen equivalent (Part A's seed-53 draw plus the drawn owners' gold documents) was considered and rejected in understand_b.json's critique. The pre-registration does not mention it.

What checks out: the earlier probe and seeds 7 and 55 are described accurately. u5kb/questions holds draws only for seeds 7 and 55 (draw_b.py). No folder outside mt5k holds the text of any unused-pool question. u5k/protocol/orig5k has no fact-bank output.
findings.fix: Add these exposures to the 'seen' paragraph. Note that v2 on the primary set uses its training wording. Replace 'only haystack' with the real reason: it is the haystack the first test promised, and it is cheap with the embedding cache. Add one line on the unseen alternative and why it was rejected (cost and disk).

verdict.reason:
I checked each claim and could not refute any of them. The finding is real, but it is a gap in a disclosure paragraph, not a flaw in the test.

1. **The development sets lie inside mt5k.** All mdtrain, mdtest, mdchanged (by document id), mdtrainall and mdtrainv9 documents are among mt5k's 5,089: 50 of 50, 49 of 49, 49 of 49, 50 of 50 and 50 of 50. These folders hold the fact bank's versions v2 to v14.

2. **The fact bank's code changed after the first test.** Commit 44a880f added the "#<pr>" alias in bank.py. The engine change is a refactor that keeps v1's default behaviour. The alias has no effect here: no question text in fb50 or in mt5k's questions.jsonl contains "#N" (the "#" appears only in gold_answer). Its storage cost is about 141 rows.

3. **v1 has already run on mt5k at 5,089 documents, on other questions.** Part A's u5k/scale/ans_v1.jsonl holds 50 multi-document questions with docs_loaded 5089, and docs/benchmarks/factbank_5k/dry_run.json has v1 differences at 5,089. Part A's pre-registration discloses this; part B's does not.

4. **v2's training wording.** understand_b.json (line 118) notes that mt5k's generated deadline questions use the word "due", the cue v2 learned. The part B pre-registration flags v2 as in-sample only for the fb50 set (line 55).

5. **The unseen alternative.** The critique in understand_b.json (lines 229, 262-263, 298) proposed Part A's seed-53 draw plus the planted gold documents of the drawn owner questions. It called this a real choice to make and disclose, ruled out mainly by about 1.5 to 1.7 hours of CPU and by disk. The pre-registration says only "It is the only haystack where owner questions with checkable answers exist". That is literally true of the haystacks that exist, but it leaves out the alternative that was weighed.

**Why it does not matter for the test:** fixing it changes no number, rule or verdict. The haystack, questions, arms and code stay the same. The deciding arm is v1, whose only behaviour change (the alias) touches no question. v2 is reported for information only. Both systems are already disclosed as having seen mt5k. It should still be fixed before freezing, as a matter of completeness.

findings.title: Rule 4 is correctly expected to fail, but the figure is a projection, not a measurement, and the range mixes in v2
findings.evidence:
Line 88 says 'On today's schema, a design probe puts the fact bank at about 0.58 to 0.64'. In understand_b.json's storage lens, the 179 MB bank is a projection: the old-schema erbfull-5000-9688c2 rows in cie_erb, minus the stored tsvector and 764 B per vector. No bank on today's schema was measured at 5,000 documents. The range 0.58 to 0.64 covers v1 (0.581 to 0.592, the arm that decides) and v2 (0.631 to 0.642).

The conclusion is sound:
- storage() counts pg_column_size of the tenant's rows plus its BM25 folder, and no indexes.
- factbank_build bytes is the whole SQLite file, its indexes included.
- Per document, the projection matches the 50-document bank on the same schema (2,029 against 2,003 B per section).
- For rule 4 to be met, bank_total would have to be at least 318 MB, 3 x 106 MB, which is about 75% above the projection.
- The 50-document figure of 0.60 (0.597) is correct.
findings.fix: Reword as: 'projected from the 5,000-document bank on the old schema, without its tsvector and with 16-bit vectors: v1 about 0.58 to 0.59 (v2 0.63 to 0.64)'.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute it. The finding is a wording problem, and every number in it checks out.

1. **The pre-registration line mixes v1 and v2.** Line 88 of cie/docs/FACTBANK_5K_B_PREREGISTRATION.md says: "On today's schema, a design probe puts the fact bank at about 0.58 to 0.64 of the bank's storage at 5,000 documents."
   - The rules section says rules 1 to 5 apply to "the fact bank v1".
   - The storage lens of cie/docs/benchmarks/factbank_5k/understand_b.json gives v1 at 0.592 (bank of 5,000 documents) and 0.581 (bank scaled to 5,089). It gives v2 at 0.642 and 0.631.
   - So 0.58 to 0.64 combines v1, the version that decides, with v2.
   - I recomputed the ratios from the probe's build.log (scratchpad/u5k/scale/build.log): v1 is 106,024,960 B and v2 is 115,023,872 B, against a bank of 179,191,242 B. The results are v1 0.592 / 0.581 and v2 0.642 / 0.631.

2. **The "today's schema" bank size is a projection, not a measurement.** The lens says this itself.
   - The 179.2 MB comes from the old-schema rows of erbfull-5000-9688c2 in cie_erb, with the stored tsvector removed and 764 B less per vector.
   - The lens's "Not checked" note says: "The bank on head layout at 5k is a projection from the old-layout rows, not a measurement." Its risks list says the same.
   - It checks the projection per row: 2,029 B per section, against 2,003 B measured at fb50.
   - "A design probe puts" hints at an estimate, but "on today's schema" reads as if that bank was measured. No such bank was built at 5,000 documents.

3. **The rest of the finding also holds.**
   - Rule 4 passes only if the bank is at least 3 × 106 MB = 318 MB. That is 1.78 times the projection, about 75% above it.
   - The 50-document figure, 0.597, is correctly given as 0.60.
   - storage() leaves out the bank's indexes, while factbank_build's bytes cover the whole SQLite file, its indexes included.

**Why it does not matter for the test.** The line only states an expectation in advance. Rule 4 is measured during the run, and storage is not re-judged against a new bar. The v1 range (0.58 to 0.59) sits inside the stated range, and either way the expectation is "not met". No number, verdict or point of fairness changes. The proposed rewording would make the line more precise.

**What I did not check.** I could not log in to Postgres, so I did not re-check the cie_erb row sizes myself. I relied on the lens's recorded figures.

findings.title: The guide to reading the rules is loose where rules 1 and 2 are most likely to be decided
findings.evidence:
Line 98: "rule 1's −0.03 means 'no question lost'". The rule is net per group: the fact bank may miss questions the bank reaches as long as it gains as many elsewhere. It fails if it trails by one question net. At 24,000 characters, chance hits can supply or remove that one question: at 5,089 documents every fb50 deadline date also appears in 3 to 95 unrelated documents (storage lens). The pre-registration lists chance hits as a known limit but does not tie them to rule 1.

It also does not say how to read rule 2 when it passes because the bank collapses while both arms are low at 2,000 characters. The probe's recalled v1 score at 2,000 characters on fb50 at 5,089 documents is about 0.23, so rule 2 needs the bank at about 0.13 or less. Nor does it say how to read plain keyword search ending up ahead of the fact bank, which was the open question in FACTBANK_RESULTS.md. Fact bank minus plain-words is reported, with no reading.
findings.fix: Say 'the fact bank may not trail the bank by one question, net'. Add the one-question sensitivity to chance hits for rule 1 in deadlines and owners, and report rule 1 with the chance-exposed questions flagged. State in advance how 'rule 2 met with both arms under about 0.3 at 2,000' and 'plain-words ahead of the fact bank' are read.

verdict.reason:
The quotes are accurate, but none of them shows a defect in the protocol.

(1) Line 98 is fine in context. Rule 1 is defined exactly on line 75 as fact bank − bank ≥ −0.03 per group. rules_b in factbank_5k_b.py lines 171-172 computes it as a difference of group means. Line 98 talks about how far one question moves its group's score (0.038 for owners with 26 questions, 0.056 for deadlines with 18). So "no question lost" is about the group score and is already net. One question lost net gives −0.038 or −0.056 and fails; trading one question for another passes. Adding the word "net" would change no verdict.

(2) Chance hits are not left out. Known limits (lines 123-125) say chance hits grow with size and name owners and deadlines as most exposed. Those are the same two groups line 98 ties to the one-question margin. The run script computes chance.json for b5k, and b_test puts both the per-question chance counts and per-question reach rows into b_report.json. So the flagging the reviewer asks for can already be done from the reported data. The 3 to 95 unrelated documents figure is real (understand_b.json), but it is about fb50, not the primary questions. And it was already turned into the disclosed limit.

(3) Rule 2: a pass with both arms low still means what the pre-stated reading says ("the fact bank's evidence still beats the memory bank's"). The rule was always a difference, inherited unchanged from the first test. The absolute levels and each arm's change from its control are reported. The reviewer's figures (about 0.23, so the bank must be at most 0.13) come from the recalled probe on the secondary fb50 set, not the primary set where rule 2 is decided.

(4) Fact bank minus plain-words is an 'also reported' number, not a decision rule. Leaving a descriptive comparison without a pre-stated reading is normal and changes nothing in the run.

Nothing here changes a number, a rule result, the replace verdict, or what evidence is collected. At most it is optional extra wording in the guide to reading the results.

findings.title: Leaving out used questions by id also drops 4 questions no test used (mt50 reuses the ids)
findings.evidence:
factbank_5k_b.py:294 builds the used set from question ids. mt50's 12 generated questions reuse mt5k ids for different questions: linear_due-001 to -005, action_due-001 to -005, linear_due_window-001, github_author-001. So mt5k questions with those ids are excluded although no test asked them.

The pools draw_questions will use are owners 47, Linear due dates 19, action items 10, and lists 42, or 32 without the flawed ones. The design's count by question text was 47, 20, 12 and 43. The action items are therefore 8 of a pool of 10.

The reverse risk does not occur: mt50's action_due-001 and -004 match mt5k action_due-027 and -015 by text, and both are already excluded by id through fb50 or fbtest. I verified with 299 draws using other seeds, never seed 61.
findings.fix: Either exclude by question text plus gold documents, or keep the id rule and state the resulting pool sizes (47, 19, 10, 32) and why four never-used questions are excluded.

verdict.reason:
I could not refute it; it checks out exactly. main() in cie/src/cie/eval/factbank_5k_b.py builds the used set from ids alone (`used = {q["id"] for d in a.used ...}`), and run_5k_b.sh passes fb50, fbtest and mt50. I compared the questions.jsonl files in scratchpad mt5k, mt50, fb50 and fbtest:
- mt5k has 243 questions with unique ids.
- All 50 fb50 questions match mt5k's by id and text.
- 44 of the 46 fbtest questions have different text under the same id. They are rewordings with the same expected answer and gold documents, so leaving them out by id is correct.
- 12 of mt50's 23 questions reuse mt5k ids for entirely different questions (different expected answers and gold documents): linear_due-001 to -005, action_due-001 to -005, linear_due_window-001, github_author-001.
- mt50's action_due-001 and -004 have the same text as mt5k's action_due-027 and -015, which are already left out through fb50 or fbtest.

Four mt5k questions are therefore dropped only because of the id collision, and none of fb50, fbtest or mt50 ever asked them: linear_due-004, action_due-001, action_due-004 and linear_due_window-001. None is in FLAWED.

Pool sizes draw_questions will use: owners 47, Linear due dates 19, action items 10, lists 42 (32 after the flawed ones). Leaving out fb50 and fbtest by id and mt50 by text gives 47, 20, 12, 43 (33). That matches understand_b.json ("122 unused: owners 47, deadlines 32 (20 Linear due dates, 12 action items), lists 43"; "8 of 12"). So the code samples 8 of 10 action items, not the 8 of 12 the design counted. The pre-registration says each part samples "questions that no earlier test used" and that "the fb50, fbtest and mt50 questions are left out". The code leaves out a slightly larger set than that.

Why it does not change the test: the extra exclusion comes from mt50's generator numbering, which has nothing to do with difficulty or outcomes. The draw stays a fair seeded sample, and no verdict or rule is biased. The pre-registration states no pool sizes, so no stated number is wrong. Its "only 2 unused pull-request lists" still holds under both counts, because github_author-001 is already left out through fb50 or fbtest. The fix is to document it (state the 47/19/10/32 pools and why the four are left out) or to switch to text-plus-gold matching before the freeze. Either is fine, but it is a description and accuracy issue, not a fairness one.

findings.title: Reported items the pre-registration lists are missing from b_report
findings.evidence: The pre-registration promises chance counts for each question, plus load and build times. run_5k_b.sh:72 computes chance.json for $WFB (fb50 at 5,089 documents), but b_test (factbank_5k_b.py:242-243) reads chance.json only from big and small. So fb50's counts never reach b_report. No chance.json is ever made for small, so that read finds nothing. measure_b reports only the storage bytes: none of load.json's load_seconds or embed_seconds, plain_meta's embed_seconds, the fact banks' build seconds, or the fact bank's storage broken down by part.
findings.fix: Read chance.json from fb as well (and run chance on WSM if wanted), and copy the load, plain and build times into each folder's measure. Or change the 'Also reported' list to match.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed by reading the code and by a synthetic probe in scratchpad/rev5kb/probe_report. I gave b_test four folders, each holding a chance.json, a load.json (load_seconds, embed_seconds), a plain_meta.json (embed_seconds) and a factbank_build.json (seconds). The report contained only chance_big and chance_small, and no timing field at all.
(1) chance: factbank_5k_b.py:242-245 reads chance.json only from big and small. The run script makes it for $W5K and $WFB (run_5k_b.sh:71-72) and never for $WSM. So in the real run, only the primary 5k counts reach b_report, and fb50's counts at 5,089 are computed but dropped.
(2) times: measure_b (lines 146-160) reads evidence_info.json storage, plus 'bytes' and 'documents' from *_build.json. It never reads load.json, plain_meta.json or the build 'seconds'. The pre-registration's 'Also reported' list promises 'the load and build times', and they are absent from b_report.json and b_report.md.
(3) storage by part is only partly missing. The bank's breakdown (bank_bytes) is reported. Plain search's breakdown is not (only plain_total). The fact bank has no breakdown in its build JSON at all, so that part of the finding is overstated.
None of this touches a rule input, a number or the verdict. Rules 1-5 use reach, direct and storage totals, and those are computed correctly. Every missing item stays on disk in the work folders: chance.json in b5kfb, load.json, plain_meta.json and the *_build.json files (copied or symlinked into $WFB). So the results write-up can report them after the run, and it is a completeness gap, not a fairness or verdict problem.

findings.title: Near-duplicate ambiguity is listed as not covered, but a quick check finds none, so it can be stated as checked
findings.evidence:
Line 129 lists near-duplicates as 'Not covered'. I checked the 47 unused owner questions and fb50's 26 owner questions (script rev5kb/owners_amb.py). I compared each gold document against every other mt5k document of the same source, by word 4-gram Jaccard over the raw record. The highest similarity was below 0.3 for every one. The only shared titles are 3 Slack channel names (138, 32 and 199 documents share them), and the question text tells those threads apart.

Deadline titles are unique in mt5k by construction. I recomputed every list question over mt5k: exactly the 10 FLAWED ids miss an item, and the rest are complete. Expected answers were computed over mt5k, so they are valid at 5,089 documents and on the gold-only small set.
findings.fix: Replace the 'not covered' line with this check and its result: no near-duplicate above 0.3 among the owners' gold documents, unique deadline titles, and FLAWED independently confirmed. Optionally run it on the drawn questions as a run step.

verdict.reason: Refuted: the "Not covered" line should stay, and the proposed "checked, none found" text would be inaccurate. I re-ran the reviewer's check (rev5kb/owners_amb.py) and got the same numbers: max word 4-gram Jaccard is below 0.3 for all 47 unused owner gold documents and fb50's 26. I also re-ran the FLAWED recomputation (rev5kb/flawed.py), and its ids match F.FLAWED exactly. But 4-gram Jaccard over the raw record only finds near-verbatim copies. It does not find the near-duplicates the limit refers to. understand_b.json:136 wrote that limit because "the 5,000-document load found 45 near-duplicate pairs", using the memory bank's own test: memory-card cosine of at least 0.92, mutual nearest neighbours (ingest/bulk.py NEAR_DUPLICATE). I read those 45 pairs from cie_erb's record_links table (read-only query, saved to rev5kb/nd/pairs.csv). All 90 of their documents are in mt5k, and one belongs to an owner question in the pool that seed 61 draws from. That question is metadata-qst_0100, "eng-platform Slack thread about cost-aware model routing with fallback ... which bot triggered the canary". Its gold document dsid_27bd877a... pairs with dsid_5075fa5a... at cosine 0.936. That second document is another eng-platform thread about routing by customer tier with model-variant fallbacks. It has a different bot (infra-bot) and also talks about a canary. The reviewer's script scored this pair near 0.0, so the check misses the real case. Looking at the text, the question is probably still answerable correctly, because only the gold thread has a bot triggering a canary and only it contains "deploy-bot". Even so, "no near-duplicate among the owners' gold documents" would be a false statement. Cross-source near-duplicates were not checked either. The current disclosure is the more accurate one. The reviewer's other claims hold (FLAWED reproduced; deadline titles unique), but they do not support the main fix. Either way this is wording in a known-limits section, so it changes no test number, verdict or fairness.
